# cb:b047 · predicate-routing-boundary

> Contracts carry routing tables; modules carry predicate implementations. The DSL expresses which predicates fire on which conditions; it does not express how predicates are implemented.

**Type:** prescription (contract-grade) · **Kind:** rule · **Domain:** system · **Status:** active
**Tags:** `dsl`, `contracts`, `architecture`, `dag-schema`
**Created:** 2026-06-09

## Invariants

- Contract rules express routing, never implementation
- Predicate bodies are implemented in Elixir (or equivalent module-resident code)
- No DAG-stored code execution - the DAG is source for what fires when, not how

## Rules

```json
{
  "given": "A new contract is being authored",
  "scenario": "The contract's rules specify which predicate fires on which condition",
  "then": "The predicate body lives in Elixir (or the equivalent target language)",
  "when": "The contract defines routing logic"
}
{
  "given": "An existing module is being ported to DSL-driven mode",
  "scenario": "Predicate bodies in the module stay in place",
  "then": "Only the routing (which predicates fire on what condition) moves to the contract",
  "when": "Ports land with module-resident predicates"
}
{
  "given": "A proposal moves predicate bodies (implementation logic) into the DAG",
  "scenario": "Any shape: inlined code, serialized AST, pseudo-DSL execution",
  "then": "The proposal is stopped and raised for adjudication per the consensus mechanism",
  "when": "The proposed change crosses the routing/implementation line"
}
```
